Mohd Arif & Ors vs The State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 31 May, 2023
 $~38
 * In The High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi

entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
+ Crl.M.C. 4112/2023
 Mohd Arif & Ors. 
 
 
 
 The State Nct Of Delhi & Anr. 
 
 
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vikas Mahajan
 
% 31.05.2023 Crl.M.A. 15460/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of FIR No. 204/2018 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at P.S. Sadar Bazar alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He submits that since the aforesaid FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have arrived at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:37:27 5.
Learned APP further apprises the court that post investigation, the chargesheet was filed by the police and the charges have also been framed.
6. All the petitioners except petitioner no. 6, as well as, the respondent no. 2 are present in person and they have been identified by the Investigating Officer, SI Praveen Kumar, P.S. Sadar Bazar.
7. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 02.04.2011 according to Muslim Rites and Ceremonies at Delhi.

sentences.text: 8. After the marriage, some differences arose between the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 which led to various litigations between them including the registration of aforesaid FIR.

9. During the pendency of the aforesaid proceedings, the parties arrived at a settlement, the terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of MoU / agreement dated 25.05.2023, which is annexed as Annexure P-3 to the present petition.
10. In the said MoU it has been recorded that the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have been living together under one roof.
11. It is further agreed that the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 shall cooperate with each other in getting aforesaid FIR quashed.

12. Having regard to the fact that the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 have started living together and they have arrived at a settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
13. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:37:27 14.
Consequently, the petition is allowed and FIR No. 204/2018 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at P.S. Sadar Bazar alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, is quashed.
15. The petition is disposed of.
16. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 31, 2023 N.S. ASWAL
